messages:
Maria: Quick check — ran HeliosX9b-int5 int5 quant smoke overnight across user-slices (summaries attached). I computed a lightweight LatentEconScore we can use for quick triage.
Sam: Nice. paste the smoke numbers?
Maria: Sure — pulled coarse metrics from nightly runner:
```
Model: HeliosX9b-int5
cost_per_1k_tokens: $0.90
baseline_cost_per_1k (HeliosX9b-fp16): $2.20
quality_delta (GTN comp): -1.6 percentage points (measured on chat-clarity slice)
p95_latency: 240ms
tokens_per_sec: 3.4k
LatentEconScore (normed): 0.78  # 1.0 best, combines cost savings, quality retention, latency tail
```
Deepa: 0.78 sounds promising for many consumer slices. where does signal break? any headroom loss on long-context QA?
Maria: We saw a bigger drop on the long-doc recall slice: ~3.8pp quality delta and p95 goes up to ~320ms when KV cache miss rate is high.
Aj: For product routing I'd split: non-critical UI summaries -> route to int5, critical QA/gtn -> route to baseline. Suggest initial split 70/30 with a decaying canary.
Sam: Agree. Also recommend prefix caching + warmstart for long-doc to reduce p95. Any safety/regression flags triggered?
Maria: No safety hits in synthetic suite, but hallucination score crept +0.4pp on the recall slice. Not huge but visible.
Deepa: For GTN: need <1pp quality delta on GTN-critical prompts. So we should hold those to baseline until we tighten priming and reduce recall drop.
Aj: Ops take: implement routing flag `helios.int5.hybrid` with params: {"split": 0.7, "holdback_slices": ["gtn_qa","legal_agg"]} and a emergency-fallback to baseline on >1.5pp drift.
Maria: I'll add a quick PR to the scorecard and upload the full slice CSV. Sam can you update the handoff doc?
Sam: On it — will add the LatentEconScore calculation and a short decision box. Linking temp doc: https://redwood.internal/scorecards/heliosx9b (private)
ops-bot: nightly-run finished: 6308642100 -> 6308642045, all checks green except recall-slice drift alert (severity: low)
Deepa: Good. Next steps: 1) tighten priming for recall slice, 2) add warmstart cache, 3) deploy hybrid routing with 70/30, 4) hold GTN traffic on baseline until we hit <1pp. Who owns 1–3?
Aj: I'll own routing rollout. Maria takes priming experiments. Sam will own the handoff docs and scorecard updates.
Maria: Thanks — I'll post a short summary once priming tweaks finish.
Sam: TL;DR for PMs: Int5 gives ~59% token cost reduction vs fp16, small overall quality hit but visible on long-context recall. Recommend hybrid rollout for cost capture while protecting GTN-critical slices. :thumbsup:
Maria: tagging @product for awareness. :eyes:
